claim: High initial target price (day-1 close over offer price) ratios are associated with significant negative abnormal returns of 3.5% over the two months following the announcement; consistent with investor overreaction.
quote: significant negative abnormal returns of 3.5% over the two months following the announcement
limitations: Working paper draft April 2015; conditions on offer price which we do not have in the 8-K pipeline; sample and cost treatment not audited here.
impact_on_spec: Direct evidence on the post-announcement window this iteration trades: a subset of targets (high price-to-offer) subsequently under-perform, so an unconditional 20/60 day hold can be diluted or negative. Motivates reporting drift by 1-20 day CAR rather than assuming positive drift.

claim: The merger arbitrage spread has declined by more than 400 bps since 2002; the decline is economically and statistically significant and part of it is likely permanent (increased arbitrage capital, reduced transaction costs).
quote: The merger arbitrage spread has declined by more than 400 bps since 2002
limitations: Sample ends around 2008-2009; does not cover 2020s; hedge-fund index returns, not stock-level next-open entries.
impact_on_spec: Explains why a plain post-announcement long in targets should earn little after our 10-20 bp per side costs: the day-1 spread already compresses most of the deal premium; only the small residual is available at next-open entry.

claim: 4,750 mergers 1963-1998: risk-arbitrage excess return about 4% per year after transaction costs and the non-linear (put-like) payoff; returns correlate with the market in downturns.
quote: After the announcement of a merger or acquisition, the target company's stock typically trades at a discount to the price offered by the acquiring company.
limitations: 1963-1998 sample, hold to resolution, hedged long-short; only the publisher page summary was read, not the full paper.
impact_on_spec: Classic upper bound for hold-to-close arbitrage: single-digit percent annual excess return with put-like tail, which is far below this workbench's admission bars once 10-20 bp per side is charged on fixed-horizon trades.

claim: Across 51,000+ US takeover-type events 1992-2021 small stocks earn disproportionately large gains BEFORE deals are announced because of less analyst coverage.
quote: smaller companies experience disproportionately large gains
limitations: Abstract only, claim_only; full text paywalled.
impact_on_spec: Warns that in the small-cap tier the bulk of the target premium may already be in the price at the 8-K; hence pre-announcement CAR must be reported and the t3 variant is a real test, not a favored bet.

claim: Merger-arbitrage excess returns are negatively related to arbitrage capital (limited arbitrage) and are economically and statistically significant in 1981-1996.
quote: negative relationship between excess returns related to merger arbitrage and the amount of arbitrage capital
limitations: SSRN returned 403; only search-engine summary and the Wikipedia/Jetley-Ji citations were read.
impact_on_spec: Supports the premise that fixed-horizon target holds can earn a premium only when arbitrage capital is scarce; recent decades have more capital, so the recent window is the fair test.

claim: Target CARs of 14-32% accrue up to and including the announcement date and start days to weeks before it (Keown-Pinkerton 7 days, Jarrell-Poulsen 15 days, Schwert 42 days).
quote: cumulative abnormal returns ranging from 14.04 to 32.35% over the period up to and including the announcement date
limitations: Search-result summary of a survey paper; the PDF (Glasgow eprint) was not opened as text.
impact_on_spec: Defines the leakage check: report the [-5,-1] CAR before the 8-K; if the premium is already earned pre-8-K there is nothing left to trade at next open.

claim: Deal break rates 8% (2,182 mergers 1990-2007) to 22.7% (1901 mergers 1981-1996); friendly deals close 82%, hostile 38%; transaction costs significantly erode arbitrage returns.
impact_on_spec: Break risk is why we do not condition on completion: DEFM14A/closing data would select survivors, so only fixed-horizon holds are tested.

claim: The SEC efts.sec.gov full-text search endpoint is free, key-less, covers 2001 onward, returns form/items/CIK/accession per hit.
quote: no key needed, coverage back to 2001
limitations: README of a third-party wrapper; fair-access User-Agent and <=10 req/s still apply.
impact_on_spec: Data source for the free EDGAR merger-agreement 8-K pipeline; confirmed locally that hits are per file with items lists.
